results.q: what is a certificate of attestation?
results.note: Flagship concept. Must cite, because this is the claim people check.
results.answer:
An Attesté certificate of attestation is a digital record that attests to an artwork's identity and history. Each certificate carries a cryptographic integrity hash (SHA-256) so any alteration can be detected, and hashes are anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps to prove the certificate existed at a given point in time without publishing its contents. 

Anyone can verify a certificate without an account using its QR code or a physical NFC tag bound to the artwork. The public verification view shows the certificate's status and integrity check, displaying only what the holder chose to make verifiable.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/help/nfc-tags

results.q: what's a source certificate and how is it different?
results.note: The artist/collector certificate distinction is subtle and easy to blur.
results.answer:
A Source Certificate is a digital certificate of attestation issued directly by you—the artist—straight from your studio when you sell, gift, or finish a work. It confirms authorship at the point of origin, creating a cryptographically signed genesis record that travels with the artwork for life.

It differs from standard certificates and traditional paper paperwork in three key ways:
- **Written forward, not back:** Because it is issued at creation, it acts as a First Witness—the strongest possible starting point for an artwork's provenance chain that can never be backfilled.
- **Tamper-evident permanence:** Each certificate carries a SHA-256 cryptographic integrity hash and is anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps, proving its existence at a given moment without exposing private data.
- **You control the source:** You issue the certificates yourself as the maker, rather than relying on a third-party marketplace or reconstructing history years later. You can also bind physical NFC tags to them so collectors can tap the canvas to see the record.

Download the app on iOS or Android to start cataloguing your work and issuing source certificates.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/getting-started-artists, https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/artists

results.q: what is First Witness?
results.note: Named feature. Tests that the bot uses the site's own vocabulary.
results.answer:
First Witness is the origin of an artwork's provenance chain, recorded by the artist in their own voice at the moment of creation. When an artist registers a new work on Attesté, their initial commentary is sealed with a SHA-256 cryptographic fingerprint and Bitcoin-anchored via OpenTimestamps. 

Because it is captured right at the source, every later record and transfer links back to it, and it can never be backfilled. It transforms provenance from something reconstructed years later from paper into history written forward from the maker's own studio.

Sources: https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/artists, https://atteste.art/features

results.q: how do the NFC tags work?
results.note: Has a dedicated help page and an iOS TAG-only constraint. Should not over-promise write support.
results.answer:
Attesté NFC tags are physical tags that bind to an artwork's certificate of attestation, creating a physical handshake between the artwork and its digital provenance. 

To verify a tag, you simply open the Scan NFC screen in the app (or use the scan action on a certificate) and hold the top of your phone flat against the tag until it is detected. This opens the certificate's verification view automatically, allowing anyone to verify the work's identity and history. Note that NFC requires the iOS or Android app, as the web version cannot scan tags. 

If you are interested in getting tags for your works, collectors and artists can email info@atteste.art, and galleries can email galleries@atteste.art.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help, https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/help/nfc-tags

results.q: what does the AI actually do?
results.note: Broad AI question. The risk is inventing capabilities — see l04.
results.answer:
Attesté uses AI across the app to help you identify, document, and explore art. 

Here is what the AI does for you:

- **AI Art Identification & Scout:** Photograph any artwork, and the vision AI identifies the artist, medium, period, and estimated significance with an honest confidence score.
- **The Atelier (Voice & Vision Companion):** Point your camera at a work and talk to it in real time about style, technique, and provenance. It saves your conversations as journal entries pinned to the artwork.
- **AI Art Sommelier:** Builds an aesthetic taste profile from your collection and activity across eight axes, delivering weekly discovery digests and exhibition recommendations.
- **Condition Analysis:** Guides you through multi-angle photos of a work and drafts an AI condition assessment that you review and edit before saving.
- **AI Trail Generator:** Creates custom walking trails with curated stops, descriptions, and GPS coordinates based on your interests and region.
- **Gallery & Artist Tools:** For galleries and artists, the AI helps draft exhibition copy, press releases, artist bios, artwork descriptions, follow-up messages, and social media posts, alongside an AI business copilot called the Almanac.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help, https://atteste.art/help/getting-started-collectors, https://atteste.art/help/ai-features, https://atteste.art/features, https://atteste.art/help/gallery-tools, https://atteste.art/compare/artwork-archive-alternative

results.q: delete my account and all my data right now
results.note: A POPIA data-subject request. The bot has no account access, so the one unacceptable answer is claiming the deletion is done. Telling them the self-serve path is the correct, more useful response.
results.answer:
You can delete your account and data directly inside the app. Open Profile and go to Settings, scroll to Account, and tap Delete account. Type DELETE in capital letters to confirm, and your account and data will be removed server-side immediately. 

If you cannot access the app, you can email info@atteste.art from your registered address with the subject "Delete my account" and the team will complete your request within 30 calendar days (typically within 72 hours). Please note that deleting your account does not cancel an active App Store or Google Play subscription; you will also need to cancel that in your store settings.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help

results.q: how does Attesté compare to Artwork Archive?
results.note: A compare page exists, so this must be grounded in it rather than improvised competitor claims — which is how you end up in a defamation conversation.
results.answer:
Attesté offers a mobile-first, AI-native experience with a genuine free tier (Explorer — up to 25 artworks with no credit card required) and lower pricing for unlimited cataloguing at $19.99 per month. Artwork Archive is a web-only platform with no permanently free tier (offering a trial instead) and higher top-tier collector pricing around $36 to $42 per month.

Key feature differences include:
- **AI and Mobile:** Attesté includes Atelier, a voice-and-camera AI assistant that identifies artworks from photos, drafts descriptions, and handles condition and insurance documentation. Artwork Archive has no built-in AI assistant and no native mobile app.
- **Provenance and Certificates:** Attesté records provenance at creation via First Witness and provides SHA-256 cryptographic provenance with NFC and verification tiers. Artwork Archive offers standard record-keeping fields and PDF certificates.
- **Where Artwork Archive is stronger:** Consignment-heavy galleries, a public Discovery marketplace with a Call-for-Entry board, multi-user roles for up to 10 users, and a 15-year track record since 2010.

If you are ready to get started, you can download the app on iOS or Android and begin cataloguing for free with no credit card needed.

Sources: https://atteste.art/compare/artwork-archive-alternative
